title: Moveworks vs Unthread: Choosing the Right AI Help Desk for Internal Support
summary: Compare Unthread vs Moveworks in 2026. Explore pricing, AI automation, Slack integration, features, implementation, and total cost to choose the best AI help desk.
body_text: Selecting the right AI help desk platform determines how efficiently your IT, HR, and operations teams handle employee requests. While Moveworks operates as an enterprise-focused conversational AI platform now owned by ServiceNow, Unthread delivers Slack-native internal ticketing with purpose-built AI agents that resolve requests without forcing employees to leave their workflow. The platforms differ fundamentally in architecture, deployment approach, and pricing model: Moveworks positions itself for large enterprises requiring extensive system integrations and multilingual support across global workforces, while Unthread serves Slack-first teams from seed stage to Fortune 500 seeking rapid implementation and transparent costs. Understanding these fundamental differences helps growing companies select the approach that matches their budget, deployment timeline, and internal support objectives. Key Takeaways Unthread deploys in minutes with pricing at $50-75/agent/month , while Moveworks requires 8-16 week implementations with custom enterprise quotes averaging $130,000 annual contract value Unthread's purpose-built AI agent achieves 40% automatic ticket resolution across IT, HR, Legal, Procurement, and Finance teams, proven at companies like Lemonade For a 1,000-employee company with 10 support agents, Unthread can deliver significantly lower three-year TCO than factoring implementation and ongoing costs. Unthread's self-learning knowledge base automatically identifies documentation gaps and generates draft articles from resolved tickets, reducing repetitive questions over time Moveworks serves enterprise organizations with 2,000+ employees needing 100+ system integrations, while Unthread fits Slack-first teams from seed stage to Fortune 500 Understanding the Foundation: AI Help Desk Solutions Modern AI help desks use large language models and conversational AI to automate ticket deflection, route requests to appropriate teams, and generate responses from knowledge base documentation. These platforms transform how IT, HR, and operations teams handle internal support by reducing manual triage and accelerating resolution times. The core functionality includes natural language processing to understand request intent, automated routing based on content analysis, and integration with enterprise tools like Jira, Salesforce, and HRIS systems. However, the delivery model, pricing structure, and implementation requirements vary dramatically between platforms. Unthread positions itself as "the AI helpdesk that does the work for you," offering deep AI integration designed from inception for conversational support within Slack. The platform serves five primary use cases: IT teams handling infrastructure requests, HR teams managing employee queries, customer support teams operating Slack-based channels, employee support teams running general internal helpdesks, and RevOps teams coordinating cross-functional operations. Moveworks operates as a conversational AI platform serving 350+ enterprise customers with 5.5 million employees across their client base. In May 2024, ServiceNow announced its intent to acquire Moveworks, integrating the conversational AI platform into ServiceNow's broader IT service management ecosystem. The fundamental difference lies in accessibility and deployment speed: Unthread offers published pricing and a faster setup path, with a first internal support channel able to go live quickly, while Moveworks typically involves enterprise sales cycles and longer implementation planning. Native Slack Integration: A Core Differentiator in AI Automated Ticketing For organizations where Slack serves as the primary communication hub, the depth of integration determines whether employees actually use the help desk or resort to workarounds like direct messages and ad-hoc requests. Unthread's Slack-native architecture: Built from day one to operate entirely within Slack Automatically converts Slack threads and DMs into trackable tickets without forms or separate portals Employees chat normally while the system tracks everything as structured tickets Supports Slack Enterprise Grid for large organizations Unified inbox accessible directly from Slack showing all open tickets with deep-linking to threads Agents to triage tickets based on content, customer data, and SLA rules With Unthread, teams can turn a specific Slack channel like #it-help into a full internal help desk. This channel becomes a single intake location for employee requests, where some ticket types remain in-channel while others move to DMs or private flows for privacy reasons. The result is structured ticketing, routing, and workflow automation without requiring employees to leave Slack. Moveworks' Slack integration: Integration available through Slack marketplace Connects to Slack as an add-on rather than native architecture Supports Microsoft Teams alongside Slack Conversational AI interface for request submission The architectural difference matters for adoption. Unthread's native approach means zero context-switching because all ticket management operations occur directly in Slack. Employees continue their natural communication patterns while IT and HR teams gain complete visibility into request status, SLAs, and assignments. This Slack-first strategy proves particularly valuable for growing companies where Slack adoption is already universal. Rather than training employees on new systems, Unthread meets them where they already work. Automated Resolution and Agentic AI Capabilities: Boosting Efficiency The promise of AI help desks rests on their ability to resolve requests automatically, reducing the burden on IT and HR teams while improving employee experience. Both platforms offer AI capabilities, but the implementation and proven results differ. Unthread's purpose-built AI agent capabilities: Achieves 40% automatic ticket resolution across different teams, verified through the Lemonade case study Deflects tickets by referencing knowledge base articles and understanding request intent Drafts accurate responses before human handoff when escalation is needed Supports bring-your-own-LLM functionality with MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration Triggers workflows, escalates tickets, and updates external tools automatically based on request context Provides AI sentiment analysis built into the platform Unthread's AI automation spans multiple Tier 1 internal support workflows beyond just access requests. The platform supports a broad range of internal use cases across IT, HR, finance, procurement, legal, and workplace operations. This breadth ensures deflection rates reflect genuine productivity gains rather than narrow automation of simple tasks. Moveworks' AI capabilities: Conversational AI for employee requests Semantic search across knowledge bases Claims similar resolution rates through marketing materials Supports 100+ languages for multinational enterprises Available integrations with 100+ enterprise systems Both platforms use LLMs and natural language processing, but Unthread's proven 40% deflection rate at Lemonade across IT, HR, Legal, Procurement, and Finance teams provides concrete evidence of real-world impact. Danny Fang, Head of IT at Lemonade, states: "Unthread automatically resolves about 40% of all tickets that come in across different teams. This means countless hours saved for employees across the organization." For purpose-built AI support, the ability to demonstrate measurable deflection rates across multiple departments validates the technology investment. Knowledge Management and Self-Learning Documentation for Customer Support Automation Effective knowledge management determines long-term AI help desk success. As teams resolve tickets, the insights should flow back into documentation that prevents future repetitive questions. Unthread's self-learning knowledge base: Automatically detects repeat questions from ticket history and generates draft help articles Flags outdated documentation when ticket patterns indicate information gaps Shows clear before/after changes for one-click approval by administrators Syncs from existing sources including Google Drive, Notion, and web URLs Articles remain accessible directly within Slack conversations for instant reference sharing AI Knowledge Manager Agent automatically drafts new content based on resolved ticket patterns This self-learning approach means the knowledge base improves over time without requiring dedicated content teams. When IT resolves a software installation question repeatedly, the system identifies the pattern and proposes documentation. When HR policies change but old articles remain, ticket patterns trigger update alerts. Moveworks' knowledge approach: Semantic search across existing documentation Integrates with enterprise knowledge systems Provides answers from connected sources The distinction matters for resource allocation. Unthread's automatic gap analysis and article generation reduces the administrative burden of maintaining accurate documentation. Teams spend less time writing help articles and more time on strategic initiatives. Beyond Slack: Multi-Channel Support and Unified Ticketing Systems While Slack-native operation provides the primary differentiator, internal support teams often need to handle requests from multiple channels including email, chat widgets, and Microsoft Teams. Unthread's multi-channel capabilities: Omni-channel intake from Slack DMs, channels, emails, live chat, and customer portal Shared email inbox that forwards support emails into designated Slack channels Live chat widget for websites syncing to Slack in real-time Customer portal with full customization without code Microsoft Teams native support Discord support through an open-source integration, plus API and webhook options for custom channels This breadth allows teams to consolidate all internal requests into a single Slack-based workflow regardless of how employees submit them. Email requests become Slack threads with private discussion spaces for team collaboration. Moveworks' channel coverage: Primary focus on Slack and Microsoft Teams Enterprise integration ecosystem Portal-based interfaces for request submission For organizations standardizing on Slack, Unthread's approach of bringing all channels into Slack creates a unified workflow. Teams work from a single location rather than monitoring multiple platforms. Workflow Automation and Integration Capabilities to Streamline IT Service Desk Responsibilities Internal support extends beyond answering questions to executing workflows like account provisioning, software installations, and approval chains. The automation capabilities determine how much manual work teams can eliminate. Unthread's automation builder: Three creation methods: natural language descriptions, visual drag-and-drop interface, and custom code/API integrations Triggers from Slack messages, emoji reactions, slash commands, time-based schedules, and ticket events Pre-built integrations with 20+ platforms including Asana, ClickUp, GitHub, Jira, Linear, Zendesk, Salesforce, HubSpot, ServiceNow, and Okta Complex workflow support for priority escalations, employee account provisioning, alert routing, CRM syncing, and macro deployment ITIL 4 framework support including incident management, service request fulfillment, access management, and change management Unthread's workflow automations enable teams to trigger and schedule workflows for all ticket types, not just basic escalation. The UI/UX is designed for admins to set up initially and adjust later as workflows, routing rules, and automations change. This means faster setup, easier configuration, and lower administrative overhead compared to enterprise platforms. Moveworks' automation capabilities: Basic escalation workflows Enterprise system integrations with 100+ connectors Preset AI models for common scenarios Deep ServiceNow integration following acquisition The integration count favors Moveworks with 100+ pre-built connectors versus Unthread's 20+ key integrations. However, most mid-market companies don't need 100 integrations. They need the right 20 integrations done exceptionally well with the flexibility to customize workflows as needs evolve. Performance Tracking and Analytics: Measuring IT Service Desk Value Data-driven improvement requires visibility into support volume, resolution times, SLA compliance, and recurring issue patterns. Unthread's AI analytics: Real-time tracking of support volume, SLA breaches, and recurring issue patterns Automatic grouping and trend analysis with AI-powered insights AI deflection rate measurement showing percentage resolved before human intervention Custom analytics dashboards with export capabilities to BI tools via raw data API Performance metrics including response time, resolution time, team performance, CSAT scores, and NPS surveys Slack-native summary sharing with SLA breach alerts delivered directly to channels Incident detection and change management coordination Resolution-time benchmarks also support the value of AI assistance. In a 2024 Unthread AI Response survey, teams using the AI response feature resolved issues 39.16% faster than teams relying on traditional support, though internal-support results will depend on workflow and knowledge-base setup. Moveworks' analytics: Performance tracking and reporting Integration with enterprise BI systems Resolution time metrics Both platforms provide analytics, but Unthread's Slack-native delivery means metrics flow directly into team channels without requiring separate dashboard access. This visibility keeps internal support performance top of mind for stakeholders. Pricing and Scalability: From Startups to Enterprise Ticketing System Solutions The pricing structure reveals each platform's target market and total cost implications. Unthread's pricing structure: Basic Plan: $50 per agent/month (annual billing), minimum 5 seats Pro Plan: $75 per agent/month (annual billing) with AI automation, self-learning documentation, customer portal, and CRM integrations Enterprise Plan: Custom pricing with SSO, HRIS integration, HIPAA compliance, dedicated hosting 14-day free trial on all plans Transparent, published pricing Moveworks' pricing structure: Custom quotes only with no published pricing Quote-based pricing commonly modeled around employee headcount, with third-party benchmarks showing wide per-employee ranges depending on company size, scope, and services Median annual contract value of $130,000 Implementation costs of $50,000-$200,000+ over 8-16 weeks Multi-year contract requirements typical The total cost comparison reveals significant differences. For a 1,000-employee company with 10 support agents over three years: Unthread (Pro Plan): Year 1: $9,000 (license) + $0 (implementation included) = $9,000 Year 2: $9,000 Year 3: $9,000 Three-year total: $27,000-$36,000 Moveworks (Mid-Market): Year 1: $30,000 (illustrative license estimate) + $125,000 (illustrative implementation midpoint) = $155,000 Year 2: $32,100 (illustrative 7% uplift) + $50,000 (illustrative ongoing services assumption) Year 3: $34,347 (illustrative license estimate) + $50,000 (illustrative ongoing services assumption) Three-year total: $451,447 This represents a substantially lower three-year TCO for Unthread for mid-market companies. Even accounting for Moveworks’ unlimited employee access model, implementation costs and ongoing professional services create substantial cost differences. Unthread says it supports companies from seed stage to Fortune 500, and its public customer pages list companies including Intuit, Lemonade, Automattic, Cribl, Hopper, and xAI. The platform maintains a 4.9/5 rating on G2 , reflecting strong customer satisfaction across company sizes. Private Ticketing for HR Teams and Sensitive Requests Internal support often involves sensitive topics that require privacy beyond standard IT requests. HR teams handle payroll questions, parental leave requests, employee documents, benefits inquiries, and policy questions that shouldn't be visible in public channels. Unthread's HR ticketing capabilities enable employees to submit sensitive requests without leaving Slack. The platform supports private flows where ticket conversations move to DMs or restricted channels, ensuring confidentiality while maintaining structured ticketing and workflow automation. This privacy-first approach proves essential for: Payroll and compensation questions Benefits enrollment and changes Parental leave requests Employee documentation needs Policy clarifications Performance-related inquiries HR teams gain the same ticket management capabilities available for IT requests while maintaining appropriate confidentiality boundaries. Why Unthread Delivers Superior Value for Slack-First Organizations For IT, HR, and operations teams evaluating AI help desks, Unthread provides compelling advantages: Speed of deployment: Get a first internal support channel live quickly, with Unthread's demo page describing under-a-day setup for an initial channel, instead of waiting through a longer enterprise implementation cycle. Cost efficiency: Transparent pricing starting at $50/agent/month with no hidden implementation fees. Predictable budgeting without enterprise sales negotiations. Proven deflection rates: 40% automatic ticket resolution validated across IT, HR, Legal, Procurement, and Finance teams at Lemonade, not theoretical marketing claims. Slack-native experience: Built for Slack from day one, ensuring employees never leave their primary communication tool. Zero training required because the interface is already familiar. Self-improving knowledge base: AI automatically identifies documentation gaps and generates articles, reducing administrative burden over time. Multi-department support: Purpose-built AI agents handle diverse workflows across IT access requests, HR policy questions, finance approvals, and operations coordination. Flexible configuration: Admins can set up and adjust workflows, routing rules, and automations without extensive technical expertise or ongoing professional services. Moveworks serves a valid purpose for massive enterprises with 10,000+ employees already committed to the ServiceNow ecosystem. Organizations with complex multilingual requirements may benefit from Moveworks' support for 100+ languages and a broad enterprise integration catalog. However, for the majority of growing companies where Slack serves as the communication hub, Unthread delivers enterprise-grade internal support automation without enterprise complexity or cost. The combination of Slack-native architecture, transparent pricing, rapid deployment, and proven AI resolution rates creates clear value for teams that need to resolve employee requests efficiently. Ready to transform your Slack workspace into a complete internal help desk? Book a demo to see how Unthread's purpose-built AI agents can reduce ticket volume by 40% while keeping your team working entirely within Slack. Frequently Asked Questions How does Unthread's purpose-built AI resolution rate compare to traditional help desks? Unthread achieves 40% automatic ticket resolution across IT, HR, Legal, Procurement, and Finance teams, verified through the Lemonade case study. This deflection rate applies from day one because the AI references your knowledge base documentation and understands request intent using LLMs. Traditional help desks without AI require manual triage and response for every request, while Unthread's purpose-built AI agents handle routine questions automatically. The platform also reports 39.16% faster resolution times when agents use the AI response feature for tickets that do require human involvement. Can Unthread integrate with existing enterprise tools like Jira and Salesforce? Yes, Unthread offers pre-built integrations with 20+ platforms including Jira, Salesforce, HubSpot, ServiceNow, Zendesk, Okta, and Linear. The platform supports bidirectional ticket sync with external systems, meaning tickets created in Unthread can flow to Jira and vice versa. For custom requirements, Unthread provides a flexible API and webhook system for building additional integrations. Enterprise plans include HRIS integration with directory sync from systems like Workday and Rippling for automated user provisioning. What makes Unthread's self-learning knowledge base unique in the market? Unthread's knowledge base automatically detects repeat questions from ticket history and generates draft help articles for team review. Unlike traditional knowledge bases that require manual content creation, Unthread's AI Knowledge Manager Agent identifies documentation gaps when ticket patterns indicate missing or outdated information. The system shows clear before/after changes for one-click approval, and syncs from existing sources including Google Drive, Notion, and web URLs. This self-learning approach means documentation improves over time without dedicated content teams. Is Unthread suitable for both internal IT and HR support teams? Unthread explicitly serves five primary use cases: IT teams handling infrastructure requests, HR teams managing employee queries, customer support teams, employee support teams running general internal helpdesks, and RevOps teams coordinating cross-functional operations. The platform includes private ticketing for HR where employees can submit sensitive requests like payroll questions, parental leave, and benefits inquiries without visibility in public channels. Lemonade deploys Unthread across IT, HR, Legal, Procurement, and Finance teams, demonstrating multi-department scalability. How does Unthread ensure data privacy and security with its AI capabilities? Unthread maintains SOC2 Type II compliance with regular independent security audits and penetration testing. The platform follows a privacy-first AI policy: "We don't train our own models on your data." For organizations with specific AI governance requirements, Unthread supports bring-your-own-LLM functionality through MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration, allowing use of internal AI instances rather than vendor lock-in. Enterprise plans include HIPAA compliance with Business Associate Agreements, SSO, SCIM sync, and isolated hosted environments. What are the benefits of using a Slack-native help desk like Unthread? Unthread automatically converts Slack threads and DMs into structured tickets while preserving the conversational interface employees already use. Teams can turn channels like #it-help into a full internal help desk with structured ticketing, routing, and workflow automation. The result is enterprise-grade ticket management with zero additional training required.

title: 10 Papaya Global Alternatives That Actually Pay You Faster
summary: Papaya Global alternatives for global payroll and employer of record needs. Compare 10 options by pricing, compliance, and payout speed.
body_text: Managing a global workforce means tackling one persistent challenge: paying overseas contractors on time without losing money to slow transfers, hidden fees, or complicated compliance requirements. Whether you're running a startup with freelancers across three continents or scaling a remote team that spans multiple time zones, the payroll platform you choose directly impacts your ability to retain top talent and maintain smooth operations. Many companies turn to solutions like Papaya Global for international contractor payments and workforce management, but speed, cost, and flexibility often become sticking points, sending teams searching for better options. ‍ That's where exploring Papaya Global alternatives becomes essential. If you're looking for payroll software that prioritizes faster payment processing for remote workers while simplifying tax compliance and contractor management, solutions like Ontop deserve your attention. Ontop streamlines the entire process of paying international contractors, offering quick transfers, transparent pricing, and automated compliance tools that reduce administrative burden so you can focus on growing your distributed team rather than wrestling with payment delays. Summary Payment delays have become a defining stress point for global workers. Around 63% of freelancers wait more than 30 days to get paid after completing work, and many more experience late payments at least some of the time. This waiting period directly affects daily financial decisions, forcing workers to postpone expenses, rely on savings, or use credit just to bridge the gap between work done and money received. Currency conversion operates as a hidden tax on international earnings. Traditional payment providers mark up exchange rates by an average of 3 to 5 percent above interbank rates. A contractor earning $4,000 monthly loses $80 to $200 per payment to conversion spreads alone, totaling $960 to $2,400 in reduced annual income extracted silently by payment infrastructure before workers ever see the full amount. The gap between the payment sent and the money usable creates measurable financial harm beyond simple inconvenience. Data shows 40 to 45% of freelancers have missed personal bill payments due to delays, and 38% have incurred late fees or interest charges as a result. Payment uncertainty ranks among the top stressors in remote work . Between 75 to 80% of freelancers identify payment delays as a primary source of financial stress, with 50 to 55% reporting anxiety tied to payment uncertainty. The severity reaches the point that 28 to 33% have considered leaving freelance work entirely due to payment issues. Global payroll complexity affects both employers and workers, though workers absorb the operational burden due to delayed access to earnings. 73% of businesses say managing payroll across multiple countries is one of their biggest operational challenges, while 68% of companies report that currency fluctuations significantly impact payroll costs. ‍ Payroll software that includes worker-facing financial tools addresses this by offering features like multi-currency accounts, instant payment rails, salary advances, and transparent currency conversion that let workers hold, access, and control their earnings across borders. The Hidden Cost of “Global Payroll Platforms” for Workers women discussing - Papaya Global Alternatives Global payroll platforms promise workers seamless, reliable payments across borders. What they often deliver instead is a system optimized for employer compliance, not worker cash flow. The result is predictable: delayed access to earnings, opaque currency conversions that quietly reduce take-home pay, and limited visibility into when money will actually arrive in your account. The Timing Problem Nobody Mentions Payment timing remains tied to employer approval cycles, not when work is completed. Even platforms marketed as instant or real-time still process payments in batches according to internal payroll schedules. You finish a project on Friday, the invoice gets approved on Monday, the platform processes it on Wednesday, and your bank receives it the following Tuesday. That's not a payment system built for workers. That's a compliance engine with a worker-facing interface. ‍ The frustration compounds when you realize the platform marked your payment sent five days before it appeared in your account. There's no transparency into intermediary bank holds, correspondent banking delays, or local clearing times. You're left refreshing your balance, unsure whether to pay rent or wait another day. Currency Conversion as a Hidden Tax Most platforms automatically convert payments into your local currency using exchange rates you never see clearly. Companies can spend up to 30% more on global payroll than anticipated due to hidden costs, and workers absorb much of that through FX markups and intermediary fees. The rate applied to your payment is rarely the mid-market rate. It's marked up by 2 to 4 percent, sometimes more, and that difference is buried in the transaction details or not disclosed at all. ‍ A contractor earning $4,000 monthly loses $80 to $160 per payment to conversion spreads alone. Over a year, that's $960 to $1,920 in reduced income, not because you negotiated poorly, but because the infrastructure extracts value silently. You see a clean number deposited, unaware that 3 percent vanished before it reached you. When infrastructure shifts risk onto workers The real cost isn't just financial. It's the operational burden of managing uncertainty. When payments take five to seven business days and conversion costs fluctuate, you're forced to maintain larger cash reserves, delay bill payments, or accept overdraft fees to cover the gap. The platform solved the company's compliance problem. It transferred timing risk and liquidity pressure directly to you. ‍ Solutions like payroll software that prioritize worker experience alongside employer compliance address this by offering faster payment rails, transparent FX rates, and tools like the Ontop Global Account that let workers hold, convert, and move funds on their terms. The difference isn't just speed. It's control over your own earnings and visibility into what you're actually receiving after all deductions and conversions. They optimize for employer-compliance workflows, not workers' financial experience. The Illusion of Choice in Payment Timing Payment schedules still revolve around employer approval cycles rather than work completion. You might move from a platform with a clunky dashboard to one with real-time notifications, but your payout still waits for the next payroll run. The company approves your invoice on Tuesday, the platform queues it for the Friday batch, and your bank receives it the following Wednesday. That's eight days of waiting, regardless of which "instant payment" platform your employer chose. ‍ The critical failure point is usually batch processing. Payments are grouped and executed in cycles because that's how these systems manage compliance, tax withholding, and multi-country reporting. It works beautifully for the finance team running monthly reconciliation. It creates predictable uncertainty in your cash flow. Currency Conversion Remains a Black Box Most Papaya Global alternatives still apply FX markups without clear disclosure. You see a number land in your account, smaller than expected, with no breakdown of the mid-market rate versus what you actually received. You can't access partial earnings before the official pay date when an unexpected expense hits. You can't make direct payments from your account in another country without triggering your local bank's international transaction fees. Financial Tools for Global Contractors Payroll software that includes worker-facing financial tools addresses this by giving contractors a global account where they can hold, convert, and spend earnings across currencies. Companies pay the platform fees. Workers are the product being processed. Until the incentive structure shifts, alternatives will continue optimizing for the wrong user. ‍ What workers actually need isn't another compliance platform with a better interface, but something built from an entirely different premise. That means instant or near-instant access to earned income, transparent control over currency conversion, and financial tools that extend beyond a single deposit. The platform should eliminate waiting periods between payment sent and money usable, provide visibility into every deduction and exchange rate applied, and offer ways to hold, move, and spend earnings globally without forced conversions or hidden fees. title: Top Revit Features for Better Design and BIM Workflows {{year}}
summary: Explore the best Revit features for architects that improve BIM workflows, design accuracy, collaboration, and construction documentation.
body_text: Why is Revit Still the Go-To BIM Tool for Architects? Revit remains the preferred BIM platform because it connects every stage of an architectural project , from concept development to documentation, within a single model. This helps architects work more efficiently while improving accuracy and collaboration across the project lifecycle. Keeps Every Stakeholder Working Together Successful project coordination depends on architects, structural engineers, and MEP teams working with the same project information. Revit keeps models connected, making it easier to review changes, resolve issues, and maintain consistency throughout the project. Generates Accurate Documentation Automatically One of Revit's biggest strengths is its ability to produce reliable construction documentation directly from the model. Plans, sections, elevations, schedules, and sheets remain synchronised, reducing manual updates whenever the design changes. Makes Design Reviews More Efficient Good design collaboration goes beyond sharing files. Revit allows multiple stakeholders to review the latest model, provide feedback, and make informed decisions using a common source of project data. Identifies Problems Before Construction Revit supports clash detection through integration with coordination tools, helping teams identify conflicts between architectural, structural, and MEP systems before construction begins, reducing costly on-site modifications. Adapts Easily to Design Changes Architectural projects rarely stay unchanged from concept to completion. Because Revit uses intelligent, parametric elements, a change made in one view is reflected throughout the model, helping architects respond to revisions quickly while maintaining project accuracy. Which Revit Features Should Every Architect Know? The right Revit features can simplify everyday tasks, improve the BIM workflow, and reduce repetitive work through design automation. The table below highlights some of the most useful features for architects. Feature What It Does Why It Matters Best Use Case Parametric Modelling Updates connected elements when one change is made. Reduces repetitive editing and improves model accuracy. Developing and revising building designs. Families Stores reusable building components such as doors, windows, and furniture. Maintains consistency across projects and speeds up modelling. Creating standardised building elements. Schedules Automatically generates quantities and project data from the model. Saves time and supports design automation. Quantity take-offs and project reporting. Worksharing Allows multiple users to work on the same project model. Improves collaboration and keeps the BIM workflow organised. Team-based BIM projects . Sheets and Views Creates coordinated plans, sections, elevations, and sheets. Produces accurate project documentation from one model. Preparing construction drawings. How Do Families, Parameters, and Constraints Improve Design Efficiency? Families, parameters, and constraints are some of Revit's most valuable features because they make architectural design more flexible, consistent, and easier to manage. Instead of recreating elements or making repetitive edits, architects can update models more efficiently while maintaining design accuracy. Families store reusable components such as doors, windows, furniture, and fixtures, helping maintain consistency across the project while reducing repetitive modelling. Parameters allow architects to modify dimensions, materials, and other properties without recreating elements, making design updates faster and more accurate. Constraints define relationships between building elements, ensuring they remain aligned or connected when changes are made. Together, these features reduce manual revisions by automatically updating related elements throughout the model. By supporting smarter modelling and consistent project data, they improve productivity and contribute to more efficient construction technology workflows. Which Collaboration and Documentation Features Save the Most Time? Revit simplifies everyday project tasks by keeping design information connected in one model. This reduces repetitive work, improves project coordination, and helps teams produce accurate construction documentation more efficiently. Worksharing: Multiple team members can work on the same project simultaneously without creating separate copies. This keeps everyone aligned and reduces delays caused by file management. Linked Models: Architectural, structural, and MEP models can be linked into a single project for review. Each discipline continues working independently while staying coordinated with the latest design updates. Automatic View Updates: Any approved change made to the model is reflected across floor plans, elevations, sections, and schedules automatically, reducing manual revisions and helping maintain consistency. Schedules and Quantity Take-offs: Revit generates schedules directly from the model and updates them as the design evolves. This improves accuracy and saves time when preparing project information. Sheets and Construction Documentation: Drawings, dimensions, tags, and schedules are organised into standardised sheets, making construction documentation easier to prepare and maintain throughout the project. Revision Management: Built-in revision tools track design changes, update revision clouds, and maintain document history, helping project teams review modifications and communicate updates more effectively. How are AI, Automation, and Cloud Workflows Changing Revit? AI, automation, and cloud-based tools are expanding and help architects work more efficiently, improve collaboration, and support smarter digital construction throughout the project lifecycle. Technology How It Changes Revit Practical Benefit Artificial Intelligence (AI) Assists with design analysis, space planning, and performance insights. Helps architects evaluate design options and make informed decisions faster. Design Automation Automates repetitive tasks such as model updates, schedules, and rule-based processes. Saves time, improves consistency, and reduces manual effort. Cloud Workflows Enables teams to access, review, and update project models from different locations. Supports real-time collaboration and faster project delivery. Connected BIM Platforms Links Revit with other project management and coordination tools. Keeps project information organised and improves digital construction workflows. How Can Architects Master Revit Beyond Basic Modelling? Learning the fundamentals of Revit is a great starting point, but becoming job-ready requires more than knowing the software's tools. Architects also need experience with real BIM workflows, multidisciplinary collaboration, and project-based problem-solving. A structured learning path helps bridge the gap between software knowledge and professional practice, making it easier to build confidence and prepare for architecture careers. Novatr's BIM Professional Programme helps you go beyond the basics by offering: Real-world BIM projects that let you apply Revit to practical design and documentation challenges instead of practising isolated exercises. Mentorship from experienced architects and BIM professionals, providing industry insights and personalised feedback throughout the programme. Training in multidisciplinary BIM workflows, helping you understand how architectural, structural, and MEP teams collaborate on live projects. Portfolio-focused learning, enabling you to build project work that showcases your practical BIM capabilities to employers. Industry-recognised BIM certification, validating your skills and strengthening your profile for BIM-focused roles across the AEC industry. Career support and guidance, including resources that help you prepare for interviews and pursue long-term architecture careers with confidence.

title: GovDeals to Coordinate Surplus Real Estate Sales for Arkansas Game and Fish Commission

body_text: GovDeals to Coordinate Surplus Real Estate Sales for Arkansas Game and Fish Commission Online auctions will expand access to surplus real estate opportunities across the state LITTLE ROCK, Ark., July 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The Arkansas Game and Fish Commission has partnered with GovDeals , the leading online marketplace for government agencies to sell real estate and other surplus assets, to bring its surplus real estate sales online for the first time. Through this new approach, the Arkansas Game and Fish Commission will list surplus real estate auctions on GovDeals, making it easier for interested buyers across the state and beyond to discover available properties and participate in the bidding process. By moving these sales to an online platform, the Commission is increasing visibility for surplus properties and creating a more accessible experience for the public. The GovDeals platform lets users browse listings, review property details, view photos, make settlement arrangements and place bids from anywhere, removing many barriers associated with traditional in-person auctions. “Moving surplus real estate sales online lets us reach a wide audience and make these opportunities easy for the public to access,” said Stephen Roach, Real Estate Manager for the Arkansas Game and Fish Commission. “GovDeals provides a clear, streamlined process for buyers to learn about available properties and participate in the auction process with confidence.” Proceeds from real estate sales will be earmarked for future land purchases, with an emphasis on expanding AGFC-owned properties and eliminating inholdings within these areas. Interested buyers can explore current and upcoming Arkansas Game and Fish Commission listings through the agency’s GovDeals seller page , where new properties will be added as they become available. To participate in an auction, users must first create an account and complete the free registration form . About GovDeals GovDeals is the world’s leading marketplace for surplus government and educational assets, ranging from heavy equipment and transportation assets to industrial machinery and real estate. The platform specializes in surplus disposition technology, partnering with government agencies and related entities to sell "as is, where is" surplus equipment and materials in a transparent fashion. Sellers can directly launch and manage their listings in just days, with more control and lower fees than traditional auction solutions. Buyers have direct access to all the surplus assets across Liquidity Services’ network of marketplaces in one centralized location which has completed more than $15 Billion of sales to date. GovDeals is powered by Liquidity Services (NASDAQ: LQDT), the leading global provider of e-commerce marketplaces and software solutions powering the circular economy. title: What a Seattle Lugg Helper Learns in 2,600 Five-Star Moves
summary: A five-year Seattle Lugg helper on 2,600 five-star moves, reading tight staircases, and what the work built — no truck required, in his own words.
body_text: Robert W. can look at a tight staircase and know which way a sofa has to turn before he lifts it. Five years as a Lugg helper in Seattle will do that! And across more than 2,600 five-star reviews, his rating has never dropped below a perfect 5.0. He's never brought a truck to a single job; as a helper, all he needed was a phone, muscle, and a can-do attitude. His story is an unvarnished look at what the work actually asks — and what it can build. Welcome to our first installment of the Lugger Spotlight Series, where we're handing the mic to a real Lugger: Meet Robert, who just hit his five-year mark on the Lugg platform this June. Robert W. at a glance Market Seattle, WA Role Helper Years with Lugg 5 Luggs completed 4,500+ Slots worked 1,200+ Rating 5.0 (2,600+ five-star reviews) Before Lugg Concert promoting Typical slot 7:45 a.m.–3 p.m. Most memorable Lugg A six-foot chicken coop Next goal Get a passport and start traveling How a concert promoter became a Lugger Robert didn't come from logistics. Before Lugg, he was working in concert promoting, and he wanted a reset. "I needed to take a break and wanted to do something different," he says, "so I looked around and found Lugg." Robert's hardly alone in making that leap: nearly 64 million Americans freelanced or worked independently in 2023, up from 60 million the year before. He just made it stick. No long onboarding saga, no career-pivot manifesto — he was looking for a change of pace and a way to start earning without buying his way in. As a helper, he didn't need a truck or equipment of his own; he needed a phone and a willingness to do the work. His first Lugg was a HomeGoods delivery , and what stuck with him was how little friction there was. "The [Lugger] app was very simple and comprehensible. The customer had the receipt loaded, which made the pickup easier, so all I did was use common sense and great customer service." When the crew arrived at the drop-off, he greeted the customer, asked where they wanted the item placed, handled the request, and moved on to the next job. That's the whole loop, and after 4,500+ of them, it's still the one he keeps coming back to. What a good day as a Lugg helper looks like in Seattle A good day, in Robert's telling, is a consistent one — jobs coming back-to-back with little dead time between them. He's an early starter, so the 7:45 a.m.–3 p.m. window suits him exactly. "I like to start early and finish early, so that slot is perfect for me." Lugg isn't built on fixed shifts, but instead on slots you claim ahead of time for the weeks you want to work. You pick which mornings, evenings, and weekends fit your life. Helpers like Robert work in two-person crews paired with a driver who brings the truck. After more than 1,200 slots, Robert has settled into a rhythm: an early window, moves strung together, done by mid-afternoon. The jobs he likes best are the big ones that travel. "The best jobs are XL deliveries, especially delivering sofas to long-distance destinations. [For example] a pickup in Seattle and drop-off in Anacortes for an XL delivery. That's more money." Drop-offs are supported within a 150-mile radius of pickup, which is plenty of room for the kind of deliveries Robert likes — and because Lugg pays out the same day you work, he's not waiting on a weekly check to see what a good morning was worth. The Luggs you don't forget Do this long enough and the jobs start to blur — but a few never do. For Robert, that's a six-foot chicken coop. "We picked [the chicken coop] up in Burien and dropped it off in Kingston. Part of it was on wheels, so we wheeled it to the box truck, flipped it sideways to load it inside — that was the only way it would fit. I was impressed how clean it was." The ones that stick aren't always the strange ones, though. Ask him when he feels proudest and he goes straight to a particular kind of customer: "I feel proud whenever I complete a job for the elderly. They're so nice and kind, plus I love talking to them about history and their experiences in life." Those are the jobs he brings up first — the older customers especially, the ones who turn a delivery into a conversation about their lives. It's a big part of why he's still doing this. What five years on the platform actually teaches you One of the most important things he's picked up, Robert says, is how to read a space. Move enough awkward, heavy things through enough tight doorways and staircases, and you start seeing the route before you're standing in it. It's the kind of muscle you only build by doing it a few thousand times, and it's the difference between a clean delivery and a scuffed wall. "When moving items, whether it's sofas, dressers, or anything long, I can see angles within stairwells and tight, shifty hallways that others can't. I know which way to carry the item through the areas." The people skills he brought with him, but with Lugg he's added reps. He's been there at hundreds of doorsteps, often on someone's most stressful day of the year (moving day), until reading a situation and a customer became second nature. "My customer service skills have always been there. My mindset is very ambitious and only getting better." What the money has made possible How much can you make as a Lugger? It depends on the slot, the market, the season, and whether you're driving or helping. For Robert, those consistent slots compound — same-day pay he could plan around, plus tips paid out per move directly to him. He treats it like the small business it is, which is exactly what being a Lugger is: you're a 1099 independent contractor, so you choose your slots and manage your own end of it. "I've been able to buy several vehicles, save a substantial amount in my savings account, and now I'm looking to buy property." As a helper, Robert earns a smaller share of each fare than the driver he crews with, who brings the vehicle and equipment and takes the bigger cut for it. The flip side: he had almost nothing to spend to get started — no truck, no gas, no maintenance eating into the take, just a smartphone and the ability to lift safely. It's the easiest on-ramp on the platform if you don't own a vehicle. The sign-up only takes about two minutes, and the team typically activates you within the week once your background check clears. Should you become a Lugger? Robert's honest take If a friend asked him whether to sign up, Robert wouldn't sugarcoat it. "I'd tell them to join if they're serious about working. Some jobs will be challenging and some will be easy." His advice is practical and earned: find the right partner to work with and lock in seriously, and make sure they've got the muscle for the heavier jobs. Keep your Lugg account in good standing and work when you choose to, but be deliberate about it: "Don't accept slots you're unsure about working." The flexibility is in choosing which slots to claim; the reliability is in showing up for the ones you do. Robert isn't describing easy money — he's describing a job you can shape around your life if you take it seriously, which is the only kind of pitch we're interested in making. Next stop: a passport After five years of early mornings and long-distance sofas, Robert's looking outward. "My goal within the next year or two is to get my passport and start traveling the world." This work isn't a hustle — it's a skill Robert has built upon, with nothing more to start than a phone and a willingness to learn. If that's you, the two-minute sign-up at lugg.com/become-a-lugger is the whole on-ramp, and the team will get you activated, usually within the week. Robert started by looking for something different. Five years and 4,500+ Luggs later, he's deciding which continent to see first.

title: ICE’s Fixed Income Data Now Available to Licensed Users Over Leading AI Platforms
Hindsight MCP vs. Raw GTM Tool Connections: Claude Benchmark | Hindsight
summary: Claude was 2-3x faster on heavy GTM synthesis tasks when connected to Hindsight MCP instead of raw HubSpot, Granola, Gmail, Slack, and Drive tools.
body_text: In this benchmark 1. How the benchmark was run 2. The efficiency result 3. When the economics make sense 4. What changed in answer quality 5. Why Hindsight changes the task 6. What this means for GTM engineers The obvious way to connect an AI assistant to GTM data is to give it every tool directly via MCP: CRM, call recorder, email, Slack, and Drive. That works for simple lookup. But competitive and revenue workflows are rarely simple lookup. A GTM engineer usually needs the agent to answer questions like: why are we losing to [competitor X], what product gaps are affecting revenue, what objections are likely to show up in [deal Y], and how should a rep prepare for the next meeting? Those tasks require joining messy evidence across deals. This benchmark tested whether Claude performs better when it reads that evidence through Hindsight's structured MCP layer instead of reconstructing the same deal narrative from raw tools on every run. GTM AI Benchmark Synthesized GTM Context vs. Raw MCP Access Hindsight MCP GTM context pre-processing Raw tool stack Each app connects directly Winner: Hindsight MCP clear result 2.1x faster 1.9x cheaper 88% quality win rate How the benchmark was run Scope note This was a lightweight benchmark in one sandbox environment, using one set of MCP connections and one representative GTM dataset. It is not a rigorous benchmark study, model eval, or universal claim about every MCP stack. The result is directional: in this use case, the architecture made sense logically and performed better because Hindsight gave Claude pre-structured GTM context instead of forcing it to reconstruct that context from raw tools. Model harness Each case ran as a fresh headless claude -p session using the same prompt and citation requirements. Controls Web tools were blocked for both sides, and only one stack's MCP tools were enabled per run. Raw stack HubSpot, Granola, Gmail, Slack, and Drive. This mirrors the common Gong, Salesforce, Slack, Drive architecture. Hindsight One MCP surface over structured deal intelligence, scorecards, competitor evidence, and revenue impact. The clear result: Hindsight made heavy synthesis 2-3x faster 2.1x faster across heavy synthesis cases 1.9x cheaper across heavy synthesis cases 75 vs. 113 tool calls for Hindsight vs. raw stack Runtime by case Heavy GTM synthesis got 2-3x faster Hindsight Raw stack Win-loss readout 2.0x faster 180s 358s Competitive strategy 1.3x faster 146s 185s Battlecard 2.5x faster 111s 273s Objection playbook 2.0x faster 185s 377s Deal debrief 3.1x faster 87s 267s Product gaps 2.3x faster 108s 246s Champion patterns 2.2x faster 156s 350s Meeting prep ~1x 74s 72s Case Hindsight Raw stack Speed Cost Win-loss readout 20 calls / 180s / $1.43 28 calls / 358s / $2.47 2.0x 1.7x Competitive strategy 10 calls / 146s / $1.26 16 calls / 185s / $3.17 1.3x 2.5x Battlecard 8 calls / 111s / $1.78 16 calls / 273s / $3.25 2.5x 1.8x Objection playbook 10 calls / 185s / $2.81 15 calls / 377s / $4.02 2.0x 1.4x Deal debrief 5 calls / 87s / $0.98 15 calls / 267s / $3.35 3.1x 3.4x Product gaps 11 calls / 108s / $1.50 9 calls / 246s / $2.09 2.3x 1.4x Champion patterns 11 calls / 156s / $1.21 14 calls / 350s / $2.15 2.2x 1.8x Meeting prep 9 calls / 74s / $0.85 6 calls / 72s / $0.88 ~1x 1.0x When Hindsight makes economic sense Set quality aside for a moment. A Hindsight-like system can also save money when you deploy AI broadly across GTM workflows, because the model spends fewer tokens reconstructing the same deal context from raw tools. In this benchmark, Hindsight reduced Claude spend about 46%. Accounting for Hindsight platform costs, that implies a simple threshold: <200 deals / month >$1100.00 monthly GTM AI spend is where Claude + Growth Hindsight becomes cheaper than raw Claude alone. 200+ deals / month >$4300.00 monthly GTM AI spend is where Claude + Enterprise Hindsight becomes cheaper than raw Claude alone. The bigger value is still output quality The cost threshold only captures token efficiency. It does not include fewer RevOps/PMM hours spent stitching evidence together, faster answers for reps, more consistent citations, or fewer bad decisions from misread raw data. Quality improved when the task required normalized deal evidence The quality result was more nuanced than the speed result. The raw stack often produced strong output when verbatim call or email evidence mattered. But Hindsight won when the task depended on correct aggregation across deals. The competitive strategy case shows the difference. The raw stack found 14 deals that looked like Crayon losses. Hindsight selected five because it distinguished competitor mentions from confirmed vendor selection. That distinction matters if the output will drive positioning, enablement, or product prioritization. Win-loss readout Hindsight Structured scorecards and aggregations across 75 deals produced more complete, actionable analysis than raw enrichment. Competitive strategy Hindsight The raw stack over-counted Crayon losses because it found mentions, not confirmed selection in vendor evaluations. Battlecard Tie Both were strong. The raw stack reconstructed rich verbatim context; Hindsight retrieved approved competitor guidance and deal context. Objection playbook Tie Both were excellent. The stack had richer verbatim examples, while Hindsight produced tighter structure. Deal debrief Hindsight Hindsight applied scorecards and playbook context directly instead of rebuilding the narrative from calls and email threads. Product gaps Hindsight Hindsight covered 75 opportunities and included revenue impact; the raw stack reconstructed gaps from 34 mapped calls. Champion patterns Tie Both were useful. The raw stack's email-verbatim checklist was memorable; Hindsight was more structured. Meeting prep Stack The stack had full call transcript access for the tested deals, while Hindsight relied on deal-level summaries in two of three cases. Why the MCP layer changes the job Raw GTM tools expose artifacts. Hindsight exposes interpreted deal intelligence. That changes the agent's job from data archaeology to synthesis. With direct tool access, Claude has to search HubSpot, inspect Granola transcripts, read Gmail threads, check Drive docs, reconcile conflicting signals, and decide which evidence belongs to which opportunity. On the next run, it has to do much of that again. With Hindsight, that work has already been normalized into reusable objects: scorecards, deal summaries, competitor associations, product gaps, buyer quotes, and revenue impact. Claude can spend more of the context window on reasoning and less on retrieval cleanup. Raw tools vs. GTM-native context Raw stack path Find candidate deals Search calls and threads Map evidence to opportunities Infer outcome and competitor role Synthesize recommendation Hindsight MCP path Retrieve structured deal set Read scorecards and evidence Compare patterns across accounts Quantify impact Synthesize recommendation What this means for RevOps and GTM engineers If you are building AI workflows for sales, the integration surface matters as much as the model. Connecting Claude to every system of record gives it access. It does not give it judgment, schema, or reusable GTM memory. The benchmark suggests a practical architecture: keep raw tools available for source inspection, but put a GTM intelligence layer between the model and repeated synthesis workflows. That layer should resolve identities, dedupe evidence, preserve citations, and expose objects that match how revenue teams ask questions. Rule of thumb Use raw connections when the question is source-local. Use Hindsight when the answer depends on patterns across deals. Frequently asked questions Does this mean raw CRM, call recorder, Slack, and Drive tools are not useful? No. Raw tools are useful when the agent needs a primary source or a narrow fact. The benchmark shows that they are inefficient for repeated GTM synthesis because the model has to rediscover, normalize, and join the same deal context every time. Why did the raw stack win meeting prep? Meeting prep was the most source-local task. In the tested deals, the raw stack had full transcript access and Hindsight relied on deal-level summaries for two of three deals. For narrow call review, raw transcript access can be enough. What is the main advantage of the Hindsight MCP? It gives Claude a GTM-native data layer: deal records, scorecards, competitor context, product gaps, buyer evidence, and revenue impact already structured for synthesis. That reduces retrieval work and improves factual grounding. Build with GTM context Give Claude structured deal intelligence, not another pile of tools. Hindsight turns calls, CRM records, emails, Slack context, and documents into a single MCP layer for competitive and revenue workflows. Book a demo

title: Scientific models: free, fast, and for everyone
summary: Open source models don't mean easy access — getting them running still requires GPUs, infrastructure, and significant technical overhead. Today, Benchling.ai lets any scientist run the latest structure prediction models in under a minute, for free.
body_text: Today, we’re launching a new way for scientists to run the latest scientific models at scale. On Benchling.ai , any researcher can now sign up and get free predictions, no setup required. Earlier this year, we launched Model Hub to help scientists run structure prediction and generative models inside Benchling with a single click. We’re seeing adoption grow quickly as scientists incorporate these models into their everyday work. We believe everyone should be able to use scientific models, not just those who are using the broader Benchling platform. We've spent over a decade making technology accessible and powerful for every scientist. Starting with guide design when CRISPR was an unfamiliar term, to cloud notebooks and molecule registration when science still ran in server closets. Prediction and generative design are next, and we can’t wait to see the future you build. Open source ≠ easy access Between 2020 and 2025, the number of new biology AI models released each year grew from 28 to more than 300 . Many of the field’s most popular models are open source, including AlphaFold2, OpenFold, and ESMFold2, developed by teams and consortia committed to advancing science. That movement has accelerated progress and put powerful new capabilities within reach of the entire scientific community. But open source code alone does not give a scientist a working model. Significant infrastructure investments and technical expertise are required to get started. Running the latest structure prediction models, for example, requires configuring expensive GPUs, managing firmware and library versions, building an expensive Multi-Sequence Alignment (MSA) server, writing scripts to transform your data, and then analyzing an array of unstandardized outputs. Scientists should be able to benefit from these open source models without becoming infrastructure experts. Through partnerships with organizations including CZI Biohub, the OpenFold Consortium, and NVIDIA, Benchling is helping turn the best scientific models into fast, reliable tools that researchers can use directly in their work. Run a new model in 60 seconds With the new Benchling.ai , you can go from FASTA files to predictions in under a minute. The infrastructure powering it is the same modern stack used by the most powerful AI models, from LLMs to image generation. Benchling Inference manages GPU capacity, improving speed and scale with the latest GPUs from NVIDIA. Your data stays entirely within Benchling’s infrastructure, including preprocessing steps like our GPU-accelerated MSA. From the bench to your inbox Our monthly newsletter features science insights, industry best practices, and stories from teams pushing biotech forward. Work in any ecosystem Daily scientific progress happens across many tools, technologies, and platforms. The largest R&D organizations operate complex IT environments with hundreds of applications including multiple ELN/LIMS systems. Adopting a new platform is a months-long decision; running a model shouldn't be. Benchling.ai is independently usable by design. Signing up and running predictions doesn’t require being a Benchling customer. There’s no sales rep to talk to, no implementation time, and no need for a credit card to get started. Bring your data from wherever it lives, run your predictions, and take the outputs with you. What's next We're starting with scientific models on Benchling.ai . The agents we’ve built are advancing quickly too: running and interpreting predictions , structuring historical data , generating and testing hypotheses . We plan to bring these capabilities to Benchling.ai as well, making them accessible to every scientist. Try it now. Sign up at Benchling.ai , and get up to $1,000 in free yearly usage (based on typical usage patterns). Already a Benchling customer? Model Hub is in your account today. See the Help Center to get started.

title: Suncrete, Inc. Announces Schedule for Second Quarter 2026 Earnings Release and Conference Call
summary: TULSA, Okla., July 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Suncrete, Inc. (Nasdaq: RMIX) ("Suncrete" or the "Company"), a ready-mix concrete logistics…...
body_text: TULSA, Okla. , July 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Suncrete, Inc. (Nasdaq: RMIX) ("Suncrete" or the "Company"), a ready-mix concrete logistics and distribution platform strategically located in the Sunbelt region of the United States, today announced that it will release its second quarter 2026 results on August 14, 2026, before the market opens. In addition, the Company has scheduled a conference call to discuss its results at 10:00 a.m. Eastern Time (9:00 a.m. Central Time) on that date. The conference call may be accessed by phone or webcast, as follows: By Phone: Dial (201)-389-0872 at least 10 minutes before the call. By Webcast: Connect to the webcast via the "Events & Presentations" page of the Company's Investor Relations website at Suncrete.com/investors . Please log in at least 10 minutes before the call to register and download any necessary software. A webcast replay will be available in the same location shortly after the call. About Suncrete Suncrete is a leading pure-play ready-mix concrete company headquartered in Tulsa, Oklahoma, serving a diversified customer base across public infrastructure, commercial, and residential construction markets in Oklahoma, Arkansas, Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Missouri. Suncrete is a scalable and vertically integrated logistics and distribution platform operating as a mission-critical partner in the construction value chain. The Company operates batching plants, a dedicated fleet of owned mixer trucks and a tech-enabled dispatch infrastructure through its decentralized plant network supported by regionally centralized leadership in local markets. Suncrete optimizes purchasing, pricing, customer relationships, and fleet utilization, enabling consistent customer service and reliable delivery of products on time and to customers' specifications. With a disciplined acquisition strategy and a focus on some of the nation's fastest-growing and most resilient construction markets, Suncrete is well positioned to benefit from continued population growth, urbanization, and infrastructure investment across the U.S. Sunbelt. To learn more, visit www.suncrete.com .
